subject: DPA Q&A: sandbox geofencing, retention windows, and deletion proof
messages:
From: Sara Lind <sara.lind@astrahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Gina Morales <gmorales@astrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Initial DPA questions: sandbox geofence + retention

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Astra's security team reviewed the hosted flows and had a couple of targeted questions for the DPA redlines:

1) Sandbox vs prod: can you confirm whether sandbox/test environments are covered by the same residency guarantee (EU-only) or are they permitted to fall back to other regions? We need explicit language for the procurement team.

2) Retention & deletion: for data submitted to the hosted API, what is the default retention window for production inputs, and do you have a separate window for ephemeral/test traffic? Do backups (snapshots) get a separate retention TTL?

3) Proof of deletion: the customer wants a certificate of deletion for sensitive data on request — will Redwood provide a deletion certificate and what evidence (logs, job IDs) will be included?

Attaching Astra's DPA questionnaire (excerpt) for reference. Can you and your legal/ops folks review and propose redline language we can take to our counsel?

Best,
Sara

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions: sandbox geofence + retention

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Laura & Neha from Legal/Privacy looped for final DPA language. Quick summary: yes, we can scope geofencing for production-only; sandboxes are normally multi-region unless a customer asks to lock them to EU. Retention and backups have separate defaults but are configurable per-customer. We can provide deletion certificates.

Details:
- Sandbox residency: by default our shared sandbox/test pool is multi-region (used for low-volume evals). For customers that require EU-only sandboxes we offer a dedicated sandbox resource that can be pinned to the EU region (this is a paid option on Dedicated/Private). We can add a DPA clause that: "Sandbox/Test environments will be isolated and geo-pinned to the Customer's chosen region where requested; otherwise sandbox traffic may be processed in Redwood-managed multi-region test pools."

- Retention windows: production input + metadata default: 30 days for primary cache and logs; 90 days for on-disk backups by default (we keep snapshots for resilience). We offer a tiered retention addendum: 30/90/180-day options or a strict "no retention" mode for sensitive customers that require ephemeral-only processing (inputs discarded immediately after response and not written to durable snapshots).

- Backups & snapshots: backups are encrypted at rest and retained per the selected retention tier. We can exclude specific customers from backups on request (again, applies to Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers require a contract-level exception).

- Proof of deletion: we can provide an erasure certificate listing the erasure job ID, time range, and affected logical tenant IDs. The certificate will reference internal job audit logs (hashes and timestamps). For cloud snapshots we provide a snapshot-deletion confirmation record. We cannot provide low-level physical disk serials but we can provide chain-of-custody logs and the playbook entry that describes the wipe procedure.

I've attached a draft redline that proposes exact DPA language for the points above. If this aligns, Laura can propose final wording.

Next steps: propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk Astra's legal team through the redlines.

-Karthik

Subject: Proposed language for retention + sandbox clause (draft)

Sara — looping in a short proposed snippet you can run past Astra counsel. We've kept the wording tight so it's easy to insert as an addendum rather than a full DPA rewrite. Quoted below is intended as a starting point.

[Proposed clause]
"1. Environment scoping:
- Production Processing: Customer data flagged as 'production' shall be processed and stored only within the Customer-designated geographic region (EU) unless Customer provides written consent to alternative processing locations.
- Sandbox/Test Processing: Customer may request a dedicated sandbox environment that is geo-pinned to the Customer-designated region for an additional infrastructure fee. Absent such request, sandbox/test traffic may be routed to Redwood-managed shared test pools which may be multi-region.

2. Retention & Backups:
- Default Production retention for request payloads and associated metadata: 30 days.
- Default Backup retention (encrypted snapshots): 90 days.
- Optional retention tiers (30/90/180 days) or an Ephemeral Processing option (no durable storage beyond response) available via addendum.

3. Erasure & Evidence:
- Upon verifiable request, Redwood shall perform logical erasure of Customer data within the agreed retention window and produce an Erasure Certificate including job ID(s), timestamps, affected logical tenant identifiers, and audit-link references.
- Physical device decommissioning will follow Redwood's documented secure disposal procedures; such procedures are available upon reasonable request and subject to redaction for security-sensitive details.

"

If that looks OK to Astra in principle, Karthik can incorporate any tweaking from their side and we'll prepare a final redline for signature.

--Laura

From: Thomas Berg <t.berg@astrahealth.com>
To: Sara Lind <sara.lind@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Gina Morales <gmorales@astrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed language for retention + sandbox clause (draft)

Thanks all. A couple follow-ups from legal/procurement:

- Proof of deletion: we expect the certificate to explicitly state whether KV caches, ephemeral in-memory state, and request traces (trace IDs/stack traces) are included or excluded. Can Redwood add a short sentence describing the scope of "logical erasure" (e.g., "includes persistent caches, indices, and encrypted snapshots; excludes ephemeral in-memory buffers unless otherwise noted").

- Logs & audit retention: what separate retention does Redwood apply to access logs and audit trails? For compliance we need at least 365-day retention available for audit logs, even if request payloads are short-lived.

- SOC 2 evidence: can you share the most recent SOC 2 Type II report, and indicate whether your deletion/playbook is covered within the scope? We will need to validate that during procurement.

Please treat the above as gating items to move the DPA forward.

-Thomas

Thomas — good asks. Short answers and action items below.

- Scope of Erasure: we will expand the clause to enumerate included artifacts: persistent caches (on-disk KV cache and indices), encrypted snapshots, object-store blobs, and derived model artifacts generated for the Customer. We will exclude ephemeral in-memory buffers and transient compute state (these are not written to durable storage). We'll add a single sentence to the redline: "Logical erasure includes removal from persistent caches, indices, object storage, and deletion of encrypted snapshots; ephemeral in-memory buffers and transient compute state are not included as they are non-durable."

- Logs & Audits: Redwood stores access logs and audit trails for 365 days by default for enterprise customers. We can extend retention up to 5 years for audit purposes upon request and provide filtered extracts for compliance audits. We'll include this as a separate clause specifying the retention period for audit logs vs payloads.

- SOC 2: we'll share the SOC 2 Type II attestation under NDA. The deletion/playbook and change-control procedures are in-scope for the report; we will provide the SOC cover letter and the relevant control mapping.

Attachments: redwood-deletion-playbook.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — this is our internal playbook excerpt showing the erasure job flow and the certificate template.

1) I'll update the redline to add the explicit erasure-scope sentence and include the audit-log retention language.
2) Neha will coordinate SOC 2 evidence delivery to your security mailbox (s-security@astrahealth.com) under the existing NDA.
3) Proposed 30-min call: Wed 16 May 2028 at 15:00 CEST (let us know if that works).

If that plan looks good I'll push the updated redline this afternoon.

Thanks,
Karthik
